title: Duplicate OwnerReferences Can Deny Service To SSA Clients
body:
### What happened?

When some actor manages to add duplicate `OwnerReferences` to an object, any other client attempting to use server-side apply to mutate the object will fail client-side.

Consider some `Service`:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  creationTimestamp: "2020-07-10T22:57:31Z"
  name: service-name
  namespace: service-namespace
  ownerReferences:
  - apiVersion: group.whatever.com/v1
    blockOwnerDeletion: false
    controller: false
    kind: SomeKind
    name: someName
    uid: 1ea7605c-001a-11ea-9a90-027feb72be7e
  - apiVersion: group.whatever.com/v1
    blockOwnerDeletion: false
    controller: false
    kind: SomeKind
    name: someName
    uid: 1ea7605c-001a-11ea-9a90-027feb72be7e
  resourceVersion: "304470743"
  uid: 8cf44d74-d698-450f-abb6-b52f3511a85b
spec:
  clusterIP: 172.30.249.81
  clusterIPs:
  - 172.30.249.81
  internalTrafficPolicy: Cluster
  ipFamilies:
  - IPv4
  ipFamilyPolicy: SingleStack
  ports:
  - port: 443
    protocol: TCP
    targetPort: 5443
  selector:
    app: whatever
  sessionAffinity: None
  type: ClusterIP
status:
  loadBalancer: {}
```

When a client attempts to send a server-side apply PATCH, client-side validation fails:

```
E0131 12:33:54.677801       1 queueinformer_operator.go:319] sync {"update" "service-namespace/service-name"} failed: failed to create manager for existing fields: failed to convert new object (service-namespace/service-name; /v1, Kind=Service) to smd typed: errors:
  .metadata.ownerReferences: duplicate entries for key [uid="1ea7605c-001a-11ea-9a90-027feb72be7e"]
  .metadata.ownerReferences: duplicate entries for key [uid="1ea7605c-001a-11ea-9a90-027feb72be7e"]
```

### What did you expect to happen?

If unique `OwnerReferences` is an invariant required of objects, perhaps we can add some ratcheting validation for objects in `etcd` that enforces it. I can't see a good reason any client would want duplicate entries, but we must have uniqueness for SSA to function here.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create a resource with a duplicate `OwnerReference` - don't use `kubectl edit` as that client will helpfully dedupe things for you. Then try using SSA.

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

### Kubernetes version

<details>

```console
$ kubectl version
Client Version: v1.29.0
Kustomize Version: v5.0.4-0.20230601165947-6ce0bf390ce3
Server Version: v1.24.0
WARNING: version difference between client (1.29) and server (1.24) exceeds the supported minor version skew of +/-1
```

</details>


### Cloud provider

<details>
none
</details>


### OS version

<details>

```console
not important
```

</details>


### Install tools

<details>
none
</details>

<details>
n/a
</details>

n/a
</details>

Does a  the problem still happen if a client uses`--force-conflicts`?

@jpbetz while trying to find a trivial reproducer to answer your question, I found this error message while trying to create such an object:

```
Warning: .metadata.ownerReferences contains duplicate entries; API server dedups owner references in 1.20+, and may reject such requests as early as 1.24; please fix your requests; duplicate UID(s) observed: 1ea7605c-001a-11ea-9a90-027feb72be7e
```

The cluster in question has been upgraded past 1.24 for years. Just to confirm - when that ratcheting validation was added, would we have expected it to also re-read and update data in `etcd`? I believe the object that tripped me up in this bug is pretty ancient. Wondering if it would have been expected that data int `etcd` would no longer be valid.

>Wondering if it would have been expected that data int etcd would no longer be valid.

We don't fix already broken data. The interaction with apply is not-great, but if ratcheting validation is already present I don't think we'll do much with this.
Yeah, makes perfect sense.
/triage accepted

somewhat related to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/120507

> somewhat related to #120507

The scenarios that trigger panic are similar(the apiserver fails to call webhook), but the log shows that the location of panic is different.

/assign @dims
For context of [`k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/filters`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/filters/OWNERS)
Thank you.
/triage accepted

again, full stack logs:
[kube-apiserver-panic.txt](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/files/14062163/kube-apiserver-panic.txt)
I'll try to test the mr: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/114189

Let me try to explain the panic - both goroutines are trying to write to the `Header` of the `ResponseWriter`

first goroutine: This request has timed out, and consequently the `timeout` filter is trying to send a `StatusGatewayTimeout` response to the caller. This is the client facing goroutine from the timeout filter.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a8a1abc25cad87333840cd7d54be2efaf31a3177/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/filters/timeout.go#L248-L261

Note that the call to `WriteHeader` is protected by a mutex, that means that if the other goroutine is using the delegated `Responsewriter` object via the `baseTimeoutWriter` adapter, then this panic should not happen.

second goroutine: let's check the other goroutine, it is also trying to write to the `Header` of the `ResponseWriter` object:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a8a1abc25cad87333840cd7d54be2efaf31a3177/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/authentication/token/cache/cached_token_authenticator.go#L138-L140

Now `warning.AddWarning` uses an unprotected version of the ResponseWriter object:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a8a1abc25cad87333840cd7d54be2efaf31a3177/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/filters/warning.go#L31-L37

The `WithWarningRecorder` filter precedes the `timeout` filter in the execution order, so the `recorder` in  `recorder := &recorder{writer: w}` is not using the thread safe `baseTimeoutWriter` implementation.

This is the order today:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a8a1abc25cad87333840cd7d54be2efaf31a3177/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/config.go#L944-L955

one quick resolution is to move the `WithWarningRecorder` after the timeout filter: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/115282, but there could be code that precedes that needs to write warning?
Also note that the panic mentioned in 115282 `Header called after Handler finished` is not as severe, it does not cause the apiserver to crash. 

For a more proper solution, i think we would want https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/114189

any thoughts? /cc @liggitt @wojtek-t

I tend to remove the timeout filter, the sooner the better, and I think the Apiserver panic is the P0-level bug, directly affecting the availability of the cluster

I have cherry-picked [pr114189](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/114189) and tested it in my cluster, and I still need to continue to observe for 1-2 days
I opened a minimal WIP fix for the warning writer in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/123034 since the timeout filter removal is a much bigger change to reason through

> I opened a minimal WIP fix for the warning writer in #123034 since the timeout filter removal is a much bigger change to reason through

thanks a lot, I will try to test and cherry-pick the above minimal WIP fix in #123034

sorry, I completely overlooked https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/115282, I only saw https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/114189 and that looked too big to take safely right now

I prefer https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/115282 to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/123034
Can we backport the fix to 1.28?

> Can we backport the fix to 1.28?

Why 1.28 specifically? I'm not aware of anything that changed in 1.28 that made this more or less prevalent. If this meets backport criteria, going to all active branches could make sense (1.27+)

nodes.title: apiserver: warning.AddWarning should not panic when request times out
nodes.body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

request handler logic that uses `warning.AddWarning` will produce the panic `Header called after Handler finished`  if it continues to run after the request times out.
net/http does not allow writing to header if it has finished running the request handler. 

I added a new test `TestWarningWithRequestTimeout` to reproduce the panic:
```

        	/home/akashem/go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/vendor/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/filters/warning_test.go:163 +0x6e
        panic({0x1524a40, 0x19ad170})
        	/usr/lib/go/src/runtime/panic.go:884 +0x212
        net/http.(*http2responseWriter).Header(0x12b?)

        k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/warning.AddWarning({0x19c7938?, 0xc0005927e0?}, {0x1753141, 0x5}, {0x17529dc, 0x4})

Notably, administrators can utilize resources like LimitRange, StorageQuota, or ResourceQuota to enforce such limitations effectively.

title: Accessing NodePort on K8S host has latency when reaching Pods across different hosts
body:
### What happened?

I have deployed a Kubernetes cluster on Debian 12.4 operating system. I am using a test image, exposing a port to obtain the container's name. I use this method to determine which Pod the request is assigned to.

As shown in the screenshot below, accessing the Pod on the local machine works fine. However, if the request is assigned to a Pod on another host, there is a 1-second delay before receiving a response. Upon inspecting the packets using tcpdump, I observed that the first request resulted in a connection reset, and I am not quite sure about the cause of this issue.

![image](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/104751498/d2fb1b0e-d2ea-4627-b691-9d6bfbc1398f)

![image](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/104751498/84aa407e-4387-47fe-94f1-384950f0909a)



### What did you expect to happen?

Deployed Kubernetes environment is functioning properly on CentOS 7.9 operating system.

![image](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/104751498/7f9ed3e6-c0be-4458-b6fd-b6c05afa6842)


### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

I can reproduce it on Debian 12, Debian 11, and Ubuntu 22.04.

Here is my YAML file.

```
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: test
  namespace: default
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: test

      - name: test
        image: centos:7.9.2009
        command:
        - sh

          echo $(hostname) > hostname.txt
          python -m SimpleHTTPServer
        resources:
          limits:
            memory: 512Mi
            cpu: 1
          requests:
            memory: 64Mi
            cpu: 0.01
        volumeMounts:
        - name: tz-config
          mountPath: /etc/localtime

        hostPath:
          path: /usr/share/zoneinfo/Etc/GMT-8

---

apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: test
  namespace: default
spec:
  selector:
    app: test
  ports:
  - name: external-test
    port: 8000
    targetPort: 8000

  type: NodePort

```

body:

	// Graceful shutdown of the pod.

title: kubectl fails to aggregate cluster role selectors when specifying multiple --aggregation-rule flags
body:
### What happened?

I've created 3 cluster roles, one that has read access to pods, one that has access to delete pods and one that will aggregate the rules between the first two. When creating the aggregator role with imperative commands, the resulted role fails to aggregate the permissions properly even with separate arguments for the aggregation rules, the issue happens because the resulted selector seems to look for roles that have a combination of all the labels instead of roles that have either of the labels. Editing the cluster role selector to look for roles that have either of the labels seems to fix the issue.

### What did you expect to happen?

Creating the cluster role that aggregates the rules should work properly with imperative commands without me having to manually edit the resource.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

This was a step by step process of me reproducing the issue:

```
kind-learning/default  k create clusterrole test --verb=get,watch,list --resource=pods                                                                          
clusterrole.rbac.authorization.k8s.io/test created

kind-learning/default  k create clusterrole test2 --verb=delete --resource=pods                                                                                 
clusterrole.rbac.authorization.k8s.io/test2 created

kind-learning/default  k label clusterrole test reader=true                                                                                                     
clusterrole.rbac.authorization.k8s.io/test labeled

kind-learning/default  k label clusterrole test2 delete=true                                                                                                    
clusterrole.rbac.authorization.k8s.io/test2 labeled

kind-learning/default  k describe clusterrole test                                                                                                              
Name:         test
Labels:       reader=true
Annotations:  <none>
PolicyRule:
  Resources  Non-Resource URLs  Resource Names  Verbs
  ---------  -----------------  --------------  -----
  pods       []                 []              [get watch list]

kind-learning/default  k describe clusterrole test2                                                                                                             
Name:         test2
Labels:       delete=true
Annotations:  <none>
PolicyRule:
  Resources  Non-Resource URLs  Resource Names  Verbs
  ---------  -----------------  --------------  -----
  pods       []                 []              [delete]

kind-learning/default  k create clusterrole test3 --aggregation-rule=reader=true --aggregation-rule=delete=true                                                
clusterrole.rbac.authorization.k8s.io/test3 created

kind-learning/default  k describe clusterrole test3                                                                                                             
Name:         test3
Labels:       <none>
Annotations:  <none>
PolicyRule:
  Resources  Non-Resource URLs  Resource Names  Verbs
  ---------  -----------------  --------------  -----
```

The issue lies in the way the cluster role is generated:

```
kind-learning/default  k get clusterrole test3 -o yaml                                                                                                          
aggregationRule:
  clusterRoleSelectors:
  - matchLabels:
      delete: "true"
      reader: "true"
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRole
metadata:
  creationTimestamp: "2024-01-14T14:19:25Z"
  name: test3
  resourceVersion: "1508"
  uid: b138a790-d2b0-4bae-9e1f-7d51179599ec
rules: null
```

The first matchLabels rule will look for roles that have both the delete=true and reader=true labels, but instead these should be separate rules, as specified in the creation of the clusterrole called test3 with two separate --aggregation-rule arguments.

Editing the cluster role to have two separate matchLabels selectors fixes the issue:

```
kind-learning/default  k edit clusterrole test3                                                                                                                 
clusterrole.rbac.authorization.k8s.io/test3 edited

kind-learning/default  k get clusterrole test3 -o yaml                                                                                                   
aggregationRule:
  clusterRoleSelectors:
  - matchLabels:
      delete: "true"
  - matchLabels:
      reader: "true"
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRole
metadata:
  creationTimestamp: "2024-01-14T14:19:25Z"
  name: test3
  resourceVersion: "2066"
  uid: b138a790-d2b0-4bae-9e1f-7d51179599ec
rules:
- apiGroups:
  - ""
  resources:
  - pods
  verbs:
  - delete
- apiGroups:
  - ""
  resources:
  - pods
  verbs:
  - get
  - watch
  - list

kind-learning/default  k describe clusterrole test3                                                                                                             
Name:         test3
Labels:       <none>
Annotations:  <none>
PolicyRule:
  Resources  Non-Resource URLs  Resource Names  Verbs
  ---------  -----------------  --------------  -----
  pods       []                 []              [delete get watch list]
```

The performed edit was this:

```
- matchLabels:
-     delete: "true"
-     reader: "true"
+ matchLabels:
+     delete: "true"
+ - matchLabels:
+     reader: "true"
```

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

### Kubernetes version

<details>

```console
$ kubectl version
Client Version: v1.29.0
Kustomize Version: v5.0.4-0.20230601165947-6ce0bf390ce3

```

</details>


### Cloud provider

No cloud provider, I am using Kind locally with the following configuration:

```
cat kind-cluster-config.yaml

kubeadmConfigPatches:

title: Mutation webhook fails with unsupported patch type error
body:
### What happened?

Patch operations on the custom resource fails when I use a mutation webhook to add an annotation. I expected "application/json-patch+json" patch type to work for mutation webhooks.

error: mycustomresources.sample.com "mycustomresource" could not be patched: Internal error occurred: failed calling webhook "mutation-webhook.myns.svc.cluster.local": unsupported patch type "application/json-patch+json"

### What did you expect to happen?

Expected kube-apiserver to apply the annotation on the custom resource.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create a CRD
Create a Custom resource
Write a mutation webhook that simply adds an annotation to the CR.
Update the custom resource using `kubectl edit`.

### Anything else we need to know?

If I do not add any annotations to the JSONPatch in my webhook code, things work fine.

nodes.body: /sig api-machinery

Figured out why this is happening. Things are working fine now.

The java client library has `V1Patch.PATCH_FORMAT_JSON_PATCH` constant value set to `application/json-patch+json` however in mutation webhooks the `patchType` needs to be set to `JSONPatch` as per this -https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/e5b64bdef7e64b0a4ef20e055afbf60674625f42/pkg/apis/admission/types.go#L154.

Thanks!
/triage accepted

title: kube-scheduler memory leak issue in v1.28.3
body:
### What happened?

We have identified a memory leak issue in kube-scheduler after upgrading to version v1.28.3. Despite a stable number of pods/nodes, we have noticed a continuous increase in kube-scheduler memory usage over time.

title: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy using CRDs as paramKind always fails after restarting kube-apiserver
body:
### What happened?

I'm using ValidatingAdmissionPolicy(VAP) with setting my own CRD to paramKind in my on-premise cluster. It works fine, but once I restarted one of the kube-apiserver instances it changed to reject both valid and invalid requests with the error message like:

```

### What did you expect to happen?

VAP using CRDs as paramKind should continue to work fine even when one of kube-apiserver instances is restarted.

@hrk091 We are experiencing the **same issue with Kubernetes v1.27.9**, but it is very flaky and does not occur all the time.

~~Have you tried enabling the feature gate `AdmissionWebhookMatchConditions` as well? After enabling it, restarting the kube-apiserver seems to work (although I have not yet analyzed the code in detail)~~

~~Edit: first I thought the feature gate is also regarding the `ValidatingAdmissionPolicy`, but it's only for validating and admission webhooks. But it seems to help with this issue here 🤷🏻‍♂️~~

Edit 2: it's totally flaky and cannot be mitigated with the `AdmissionWebhookMatchConditions` feature gate 😞. Sometimes a single restart of the kube-apiserver fixes this bug again, sometimes it needs multiple restarts.

cc @cici37 @alexzielenski 

I don't think we should go to GA without a fix for this.

How long does this condition last for you? The param CRD is checked when the policy is resynced as you said. 
The controller is written so that if an error is returned from looking up the param resource it retries again later, so the manual resync shouldn't be necessary. But it does use exponential backoff:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7bb00356f06332e63a9f06acd42f1bdd8fc559d6/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/admission/plugin/validatingadmissionpolicy/controller_reconcile.go#L248-L259

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7bb00356f06332e63a9f06acd42f1bdd8fc559d6/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/admission/plugin/validatingadmissionpolicy/internal/generic/controller.go#L245-L254

I'd be curious if you have more logs, specifically around lines from the controller automatic resync that include "error syncing"


Additionally, the RESTMapper used to perform this check is refreshed every 30 seconds, so there could be up to a 30s delay at least after a CRD is added that it becomes visible (assuming no rate limit):

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/049614f884e61d87fc5e277cf9fd7cb2e6571217/pkg/kubeapiserver/admission/config.go#L66-L78

```

```

After all, I deleted and recreated the validatingAdmissionPolicy then it recovered to execute validation correctly.

```
❯ kubectl delete validatingadmissionpolicies.admissionregistration.k8s.io test-vap 

❯ cat << EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy
metadata:
  name: test-vap
spec:
  failurePolicy: Fail
  paramKind:
    apiVersion: example.com/v1alpha1
    kind: Foo
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
    - apiGroups: ["rbac.authorization.k8s.io"]
      apiVersions: ["v1"]
      operations: ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
      resources: ["rolebindings"]
  validations:
  - expression: "object.subjects.all(s, s.name == params.spec.foo)"
    messageExpression: "'subject must be ' + string(params.spec.foo)"
EOF
validatingadmissionpolicy.admissionregistration.k8s.io/test-vap created

❯ kubectl create rolebinding view --clusterrole=view --group=foo -n test
rolebinding.rbac.authorization.k8s.io/view created
```

Thanks @hrk091 for your detailed report! From this I think I may have found the source of the issue. It was curious to me that your logs only contained a single occurrance of:

> E0125 12:51:58.936371       1 controller.go:258] error syncing 'test-vap': failed to find resource referenced by paramKind: 'example.com/v1alpha1, Kind=Foo', requeuing

This indicates to me that it was not retrying correctly. Snooping around the code I see this line added to the top of `reconcilePolicyDefinitionSpec`:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2363cdcc399cbf428210efb2c51575ddcad2b84a/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/admission/plugin/validatingadmissionpolicy/controller_reconcile.go#L183-L188

This short circuits the resync since the spec did not change. 

I was able to reproduce your bug report in an integration test, and with a small code change I now see the policy syncing retried multiple times (with exponential backoff) until success after restarting the apiserver:

```

E0126 18:51:04.419327   92720 controller.go:258] error syncing 'allowed-prefixes': failed to find resource referenced by paramKind: 'cr.bar.com/v1, Kind=Foo', requeuing
...
I0126 18:51:35.146816   92720 controller.go:99] starting &ParamKind{APIVersion:cr.bar.com/v1,Kind:Foo,}-controller
I0126 18:51:35.146849   92720 shared_informer.go:311] Waiting for caches to sync for &ParamKind{APIVersion:cr.bar.com/v1,Kind:Foo,}-controller
I0126 18:51:35.246959   92720 shared_informer.go:318] Caches are synced for &ParamKind{APIVersion:cr.bar.com/v1,Kind:Foo,}-controller
I0126 18:51:35.246975   92720 controller.go:194] Started 1 workers for &ParamKind{APIVersion:cr.bar.com/v1,Kind:Foo,}-controller
```

code change and test here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/123003

@alexzielenski thanks a lot for the fix.
Unfortunately, it will take a lot of time until this arrives to the distro that we are using. As we already rely on VAP for some policy enforcement, we would like to understand if there would be any simple workaround that can help when this issue happens (apart from restart the API several times when it gets fixed...).
@Cajga backport PR is already created, see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/123080

@tobiasgiese thanks. Yes, just realized it after I wrote my comment.
Until that arrives to the distros, what would be the simplet/best way to "trigger" a sync manually to "get rid of the issue" when it happens? Seems deleting the VAP, VAPB and CRD and re-apply them removes the issue... Is there any better way?

nodes.title: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy: dont skip reconcile for unchanged policy if last sync failed
nodes.body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

There is logic in VAP's reconcile for a policy which short circuits if the policy is unchanged. However, we rely on resync to retry creating the policy's param informer. This change makes it so if the paramKind is unsuccessfully synced, the sync is retried.

title: confusing CRI-O error from cadvisor for nodes that use containerd
body:
### What happened?

After a fresh installation of CentOS Stream 9 with Kubernetes, I am encountering a registration failure for the CRI-O container factory. The error message indicates a problem with connecting to the CRI-O socket: Get "http://%2Fvar%2Frun%2Fcrio%2Fcrio.sock/info": dial unix /var/run/crio/crio.sock: connect: no such file or directory. Despite not having CRI-O installed and using Containerd, Kubernetes is attempting to register the CRI-O container factory, resulting in the failure.

- `kubelet` is starting successfully, but there is an error related to CRI-O in the logs.
- `containerd` is running without any apparent issues.
- CNI configuration for Calico is present in `/etc/cni/net.d`.
- CNI binaries are available in `/opt/cni/bin`.
- The `kubeadm-config-custom.yaml` and related configuration files seem to be correctly configured for containerd.
- The configuration for `containerd` in `/etc/containerd/config.toml` also appears to be correct.
- The `crictl` configuration in `/etc/crictl.yaml` specifies the correct runtime endpoint.

```
$ systemctl status kubelet.service

Jan 07 18:34:33 k8s-control-plane-1 kubelet[25417]: I0107 18:34:33.946014   25417 status_manager.go:217] "Starting to sync pod status with apiserver"
Jan 07 18:34:33 k8s-control-plane-1 kubelet[25417]: I0107 18:34:33.946027   25417 kubelet.go:2329] "Starting kubelet main sync loop"
Jan 07 18:34:33 k8s-control-plane-1 kubelet[25417]: E0107 18:34:33.946075   25417 kubelet.go:2353] "Skipping pod synchronization" err="[container runtime status check may not have completed yet, PLEG is not healthy: pleg has yet to be successful]"
Jan 07 18:34:33 k8s-control-plane-1 kubelet[25417]: I0107 18:34:33.947489   25417 factory.go:221] Registration of the systemd container factory successfully
Jan 07 18:34:33 k8s-control-plane-1 kubelet[25417]: I0107 18:34:33.947624   25417 factory.go:219] Registration of the crio container factory failed: Get "http://%2Fvar%2Frun%2Fcrio%2Fcrio.sock/info": dial unix /var/run/crio/crio.sock: connect: no such file or directory
Jan 07 18:34:33 k8s-control-plane-1 kubelet[25417]: I0107 18:34:33.951631   25417 factory.go:221] Registration of the containerd container factory successfully
```

### What did you expect to happen?

I expected a clean Kubernetes installation without errors related to CRI-O, as CRI-O was not prior installed and configuration set accordingly.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Perform a fresh installation of CentOS Stream 9 with Kubernetes (sudo kubeadm init --config /etc/kubernetes/kubam-config-custom.yaml), kubectl, Containerd, Runc, CNI Plugins, and Calico. Check the status of the kubelet.service and observe the error related to CRI-O container factory registration.

### Anything else we need to know?

title: E2E test is not setting the EndpointSlices conditions to ready
body:
The test create custome EndpointSlices to validate some behaviors sending traffic, so it is clear that it expects the EndpointSlices to be ready, 

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b529e6ff1c7edb3bb1eaca185b9662d8e42ac2d0/test/e2e/network/endpointslice.go#L698-L712

The API doc is vague about this situation and leaves room to interpret the "unknown behavior", quoting @danwinship

> I was going to say that the API docs say that Ready: nil means it is ready, but actually it says "A nil value indicates an unknown state. In most cases consumers should interpret this unknown state as ready". FTR, kube-proxy interprets nil as true for Ready and Serving, and false for Terminating. It's possible we should update the API docs to make that official. Or if not, probably we should change the e2e tests to not rely on undefined values

Since the test expects the EndpointSlices to be Ready we should set them, if we decide to change the API behavior, then we should add an additional e2e test to validate this behavior, but not use the same test to validate two different things

/kind bug
/kind failing-testing
/sig network

Slack thread https://kubernetes.slack.com/archives/C09QYUH5W/p1704500806325289

title: `--proxy-mode=nftables` fails if non-canonical (but standardized) IPv6 addresses are used
body:
### What happened?

When a non-canonical IPv6 address, e.g. `fd00::10.0.0.34`, is used as a loadBalancerIP, communication fails.

/sig network
/area kube-proxy

### What did you expect to happen?

Addresses like `fd00::10.0.0.34` should work, as they do for proxy-mode ipvs and iptables

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create a dual-stack service with type loadBalancer
2. Assign a non-canonical ipv6 loadBalancerIP
3. Try to access the service with the non-canonical ipv6 address

I will add a manifest for test, and more instructions later.

### Anything else we need to know?

What "canonical" really is can be debated. The [rfc5952](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5952) seems to accept "embedded ipv4", as long as the prefix follows the rules. So, as I understand it, `fd00::10.0.0.34` *is* a canonical IPv6 address.

@danwinship If you don't mind I would like to take a shot at this myself to get acquainted with the code

### Kubernetes version

v1.29.0

### Cloud provider

None

### OS version

Linux

### Install tools

None

### Container runtime (CRI) and version (if applicable)

N/A (cri-o)

### Related plugins (CNI, CSI, ...) and versions (if applicable)

N/A (but tested with calico and flannel)

nodes.body:
Use the manifest below, and the [assign-lb-ip](https://github.com/Nordix/assign-lb-ip) tool:
```
kubectl create namespace alpine-nc
kubectl create -n alpine-nc -f alpine-nc.yaml
assign-lb-ip -n alpine-nc -svc alpine-nc -ip 203.0.113.1,2001:db8::203.0.113.1
echo | nc 203.0.113.1 7007
echo | nc 2001:db8::203.0.113.1 7007
```
The loadBalancerIPs are taken from the documentation ranges, specified in [rfc5737](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5737) and [rfc3849](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3849).

<details><summary>alpine-nc.yaml</summary>

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: alpine-nc
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: alpine-nc
  replicas: 4
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: alpine-nc
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: alpine
        image: alpine:latest
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        command: ["nc", "-lk", "-p", "7007", "-e", "hostname"]
        ports:
        - name: nc
          containerPort: 7007
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: alpine-nc
spec:
  ipFamilyPolicy: RequireDualStack
  selector:
    app: alpine-nc
  type: LoadBalancer
  ports:
  - port: 7007
    name: nc
```

</details>
/assign @danwinship

If you are using KinD, you can set static routes to your control-plane for testing (--name default assumed below):
```
ipv4=$(docker inspect default-control-plane | jq -r .[0].NetworkSettings.Networks.kind.IPAddress)
sudo ip ro replace 203.0.113.0/24 via $ipv4
ipv6=$(docker inspect default-control-plane | jq -r .[0].NetworkSettings.Networks.kind.GlobalIPv6Address)
sudo ip -6 ro replace 2001:db8::203.0.113.0/120 via $ipv6
```
Since the addresses are reserved for documentation, it shouldn't disturb your network setup (in theory :smile: )

> What "canonical" really is can be debated. The [rfc5952](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5952) seems to accept "embedded ipv4", as long as the prefix follows the rules. So, as I understand it, `fd00::10.0.0.34` _is_ a canonical IPv6 address.

No, `fd00::10.0.0.34` is a _valid_ IPv6 address, but it's not "canonical" because it can't be "distinguished as having IPv4 addresses embedded in the lower 32 bits solely from the address field through the use of a well-known prefix" (RFC 5932 §5). (IOW, `fd00::/96` isn't one of the prefixes that is normally used with embedded IPv4 addresses, so the _canonical_ representation of an address that starts with `fd00::/96` doesn't have an embedded IPv4 address. It should be `fd00::a00:22`.)

But anyway, that said, it seems like this could only be failing if the nftables CLI doesn't handle those IPs (which would be a bug in nftables), _and_ kube-proxy is directly passing the value from the Service object to nftables, which it shouldn't be doing anyway because of the whole "IPv4 with leading 0s" fiasco. (I _just_ wrote [a warning about this](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/122549/commits/938721a88393b65cf9126538f06642b852d7a856#diff-f4b3c1b088debfb8229ad7432d5f86310c531d3c9c4a2e8f3cdba9bf665f01c0R104-R110) in another PR!). We should be parsing-and-restringifying the IP from the Service and passing the restringified version to external APIs. (The service tracker code enforces this for ClusterIP but it looks like we're not doing that for other Service/Endpoint IPs...)

> @danwinship If you don't mind I would like to take a shot at this myself to get acquainted with the code

Go ahead, but as above, I think the fixes will be in `pkg/proxy`, not `pkg/proxy/nftables` specifically.

+1 to Dan's opinion on canonicalizing everything before plumbing it down

>  it seems like this could only be failing if the nftables CLI doesn't handle those IPs (which would be a bug in nftables)

@uablrek you should see in the logs if it fails in nftables , because we should open a bug there if that is the problem

/triage accepted
/assign @uablrek

> you should see in the logs if it fails in nftables , because we should open a bug there if that is the problem

Yes.
```
E0106 05:36:20.530237     365 proxier.go:1564] "nftables sync failed" err=<
        /dev/stdin:73:50-55: Error: syntax error, unexpected string, expecting comma or '}'
        add element ip6 kube-proxy service-ips { fd00::10.0.0.3 . tcp . 7007 : goto external-45IHSLOA-default/alpine/tcp/nc }
                                                         ^^^^^^
 >
I0106 05:36:20.530298     365 proxier.go:958] "Sync failed" retryingTime="30s"
```

Also manually tested with the latest `nft` 1.0.9:
```
nft -v
nftables v1.0.9 (Old Doc Yak #3)
nft add table ip6 test6
nft 'add chain ip6 test6 test6 { type filter hook prerouting priority 0; }'
nft insert rule ip6 test6 test6 ip6 saddr fd00::10.0.0.1 log
Error: syntax error, unexpected log
insert rule ip6 test6 test6 ip6 saddr fd00::10.0.0.1 log

nft insert rule ip6 test6 test6 ip6 saddr fd00::a00:1 log
nft list table ip6 test6
table ip6 test6 {
        chain test6 {
                type filter hook prerouting priority filter; policy accept;
                ip6 saddr fd00::a00:1 log
        }
}
nft delete table ip6 test6
```

If a user specifies `externalIPs` with "fd00::10.0.0.1", _then every sync for ipv6 will fail_ until the address is removed. So, services added after that will not work for ipv6, and on a reboot, ipv6 services may not work at all.
/retitle `--proxy-mode=nftables` fails if non-canonical (but standardized) IPv6 addresses are used
opened a bug in netfilter https://bugzilla.netfilter.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1730 so community can fix it there

A more relaxed regexp for ip6addr may be used. The address is parsed later on anyway. Just try a ipv4 "900.900.900.0". It's recognized as an ip4addr, but can't be used (obviously), and the error points (correctly) at the address, not at the "action" as with an embedded ipv4. BTW, I tried to alter the scanner.l, but it didn't work. I don't know enough about flex.

title: kubectl auth can-i command behaviour is wrong for impersonated users
body:
### What happened?

The kubectl auth can-i command behaves differently when using the --user and --as options.
The --as option only checks the explicit permissions granted to the user via roles and bindings. It does not check the permissions which a user acquires through its associated group.
The --user option works correctly (provided the user is in the kubeconfig file)

### What did you expect to happen?

The --as option should also check the permissions that a user acquires through its associated group.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Either a minikube or kubeadm cluster with kubectl installed. openssl is needed to generate CSRs.

1. Create a new `clusterrolebinding` that binds the `cluster-admin` role to a new dummy group called `example-masters`
```
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRoleBinding
metadata:
  name: example-cluster-admin
roleRef:
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: cluster-admin
subjects:
- apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
  kind: Group
  name: example:masters
EOF
```

2. Create a new user and associate it with the `example:masters` group
```
openssl genrsa -out poweruser.key 2048
openssl req -new -key poweruser.key -out poweruser.csr -subj "/CN=poweruser/O=example:masters"
```

3. Get the base64 encoded output of the csr
cat poweruser.csr | base64 | tr -d "\n"

4. Create a new certificatesigningrequest by passing the base64 output
```
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: certificates.k8s.io/v1
kind: CertificateSigningRequest
metadata:
  name: poweruser
spec:
  request: 
  signerName: kubernetes.io/kube-apiserver-client
  expirationSeconds: 86400  # one day
  usages:
  - client auth
EOF
```

5. Approve the CSR
`kubectl certificate approve poweruser`

6. Extract the certificate in a file called poweruser.crt
`kubectl get csr poweruser -o jsonpath='{.status.certificate}'| base64 -d > poweruser.crt`

7. Add the new credentials to the kubeconfig
`kubectl config set-credentials poweruser --client-key=poweruser.key --client-certificate=poweruser.crt --embed-certs=true`

8. Add a new context
`kubectl config set-context poweruser --cluster=minikube --user=poweruser`

9. Try the kubectl auth can-i command to verify the permissions on the new user by passing the --user option
```
kubectl auth can-i create pods --user=poweruser
yes
```
This is the correct output as the user has cluster-admin permission via the example:masters group.

10. Try the kubectl auth can-i command to verify the permissions on the new user by passing the --as option
```
kubectl auth can-i create pods --as=poweruser
no
```
**_This result is not as per expectation. The logical output should have been ```yes``` as ```poweruser``` has the cluster-admin role via the example:masters group._** 

11. We can prove this by actually performing an action to create a pod by acting as the poweruser
Switch to the context just created
`kubectl config use-context poweruser`

12. Try to create a pod and it is successful.
`kubectl run nginx-poweruser --image=nginx`

```
kubectl get pod nginx-poweruser 
NAME              READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
nginx-poweruser   1/1     Running   0          26s
```



### Anything else we need to know?

This is reproducible on a minikube cluster as well as a cluster created through kubeadm.

### Kubernetes version

<details>

```console
$ kubectl version
# paste output here

Client Version: v1.29.0
Kustomize Version: v5.0.4-0.20230601165947-6ce0bf390ce3

title: kube-scheduler extender.IsIgnorable() is not work for bind path
body:
### What happened?

I use extenders to add webhook for default-scheduler:
```
extenders:
- enableHTTPS: false
  filterVerb: filter
  bindVerb: bind
  weight: 1
  httpTimeout: 0s
  nodeCacheCapable: true
  ignorable: true
  urlPrefix: http://10.108.198.121:9040/v1
```
And set `ignorable: true` to ignore scheuler error when scheduler extender is not working.
But I got an error: `Post "http://10.108.198.121:9040/v1/bind": dial tcp 10.108.198.121:9040: connect: connection timed out`.

I suppose  `ignorable` work fine in predicate path, but not work fine in bind path.

The Ignorable logic in kube-scheduler:
_pkg/scheduler/schedule_one.go: 637:_
```go
...
		feasibleList, failedMap, failedAndUnresolvableMap, err := extender.Filter(pod, feasibleNodes)
		if err != nil {
			if extender.IsIgnorable() {
				logger.Info("Skipping extender as it returned error and has ignorable flag set", "extender", extender, "err", err)
				continue
			}
			return nil, err
		}
...
```
and,
_pkg/scheduler/schedule_one.go: 905:_
```go
...
func (sched *Scheduler) extendersBinding(pod *v1.Pod, node string) (bool, error) {
	for _, extender := range sched.Extenders {
		if !extender.IsBinder() || !extender.IsInterested(pod) {

	return false, nil
}
...

the `ignorable` is not judge in `extendersBinding`.

title: Topology Aware Routing: Unable to allocate minimum required endpoints to each zone without exceeding overload threshold
body:
### What happened?

Given that we have 3 availability zones and even spread of nodes/CPU across all of those topology domains, we end up with a cpu ratio of `[0.333, 0.333, 0.333]`

Given that the workload has `HorizontalPodAutoscaler`, it can scale up and down with random assignment to zones but never with a skew of more than 1.

The workload had a spread of `[4, 4, 3]` across topology domains (a total of 11 `Pods` / `EndPoints`). This leads to an error of `Unable to allocate minimum required endpoints to each zone without exceeding overload threshold (11 endpoints, 3 zones)`

Given the [code logic here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/755b4e2bc493518f916e1b1ba11652a44b9fdc58/staging/src/k8s.io/endpointslice/topologycache/topologycache.go#L315C46-L331):
- `cpuRatiosByZone` of `[0.333, 0.333, 0.333]`
- `numEndpoints` of 11
- => `remainingMinEndpoints` ends up being `-1`
- => removes hints

![image](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/9448877/f10b8d01-44c6-4b14-b145-f706df94dc3b)



### What did you expect to happen?

Spread of `[4, 4, 3]` is capable of handling same zone traffic so I would expect the hints to not be removed.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

- Set up nodes across 3 zones
- Setup a Deployment or StatefulSet with 9 replicas evenly spread across zones (can use `topologySpreadConstraints` of `DoNotSchedule` with `topology.kubernetes.io/zone` key and `maxSkew` of 1)
- Observe a spread of `[3, 3, 3]` across zones
- Observe that hints are created
- Scale to 11 replicas to force a spread of `[4, 4, 3]`
- Observe that hints are removed

### Anything else we need to know?

title: False MountVolume.NodeExpandVolume failure warning message for readOnly pods
body:
### What happened?

Created a RWX volume and mounted it on a pod having readOnly flag set to true.

While the volume provisioning happened successfully, we did observe some warning message on describing the pod:

`Warning  FileSystemResizeFailed  27m   kubelet                  MountVolume.NodeExpandVolume failed for volume "pvc-d766a8a5-a6ba-49f4-a560-0c5e15b4ab74" requested read-only file system
 `

It seems like this message is being triggered from here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/volume/util/operationexecutor/operation_generator.go#L2079


But we never did an expand volume call, so we should not be seeing warning message. It can be confusing to see this warning message.

### What did you expect to happen?

The warning message should not be displayed when expand volume was not even called.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create a RWX volume and mount it on a pod with readOnly flag set to true. Wait for a few minutes and describe the pod.

title: Already API-evicted Pods do not get evicted by the kubelet eviction manager (memory pressure, ephemeral storage pressure)
body:
### What happened?

When pods have a long _terminationGracePeriod_ and get evicted by downscaling or some other reason (via API) the eviction is initiated which respects that long _terminationGracePeriod_. This works fine.

If the pods need to be evicted due to memory pressure on the node after the already initiated API eviction there is no more eviction done with the specified _evictionMaxPodGracePeriod_ of the kubelet. This means that the second eviction due to e.g. memory pressure cannot be successful at all when you have large _terminationGracePeriod_ on your pod and there was a prior unrelated API eviction.

![image](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/28532557/9d83248f-7dfe-49b0-88b0-7b7e9f73faf6)


### What did you expect to happen?

The eviction manager triggered eviction due to memory pressure should still be issued with the specified _evictionMaxPodGracePeriod_ even if there was a prior API based eviction with a large terminationGracePeriod.



### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

- Create a workload pod that does ignore sig-terms
- Specify a large _terminationGracePeriod_ for that pod, do not set any memory limits for the pod
- Specify a small _evictionMaxPodGracePeriod_ for the kubelet on the node
- API evict the Pod
- Make sure the kubelet wants to evict the pod (e.g. by allocating memory inside pod until the node is under memory pressure)


### Anything else we need to know?

The bug was not present in k8s 1.25.x

### Kubernetes version

<details>

1.26.7

### Cloud provider

Yes, I was able to reproduce it with this minimal example. I had 16GB Nodes (RAM) inside the cluster. If your nodes are smaller or larger you have to adjust the memory allocation in order to trigger the memory pressure eviction.


- Kubelet settings:
```
kubelet:
            evictionMaxPodGracePeriod: 20
            evictionSoft:
              memoryAvailable: 25%
            evictionSoftGracePeriod:
              memoryAvailable: 1m0s

```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:

spec:
  containers:
    - name: worker
      image: eu.gcr.io/gardener-project/gardener/ops-toolbelt:latest
      command:
        - bash 
        - -c
        - while true; do echo $(date); sleep 5d; done
      resources:
        requests:
          memory: "2Gi"
          cpu: "0.5"
  terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 3600
```



### Steps to reproduce
1. Create pod
2. API-Evict pod (e.g. via `kubectl delete eviction-pod -n default`)
3. `kubectl exec -it eviction-pod -n default -- bash`
4. `cat <(head -c 10000m /dev/zero) <(sleep 10000) | tail`
5. Wait some time

Result: Pod will not get killed by the kubelet eviction manager. If you do the exact same without API evicting the pod in the second step, the kubelet eviction will work.

### What did you expect to happen?

the `defaultCpuSet` in cpu_manager_state should be "0-3, 36-43,76-79"

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

create multiple guaranteed pods with initConatiner in a machine with 2 numa nodes.(only happens when container allocated CPUs not align with initContainer reusable CPUs)

### Anything else we need to know?

I add some logs in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/cm/cpumanager/policy_static.go#L391

- the assignableCPUs are "18-19,34-39,57-59,73-79" 
- the allocated CPU for container-2 are "18-19,34-35,57-59,74-75"
- the `defaultCpuSet` in cpu_manager_state will be updated to "0-3,38-43,78-79", which is unexpeted.

We can also get more info from both logs:
- when the init-container-2's cpu being marked as reusable, the `defaultCpuSet` has not been updated
- when the container-2 updated the `defaultCpuSet` based on `last defaultCpuSet` - `container-2 allocated CPU`([related code](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/cm/cpumanager/policy_static.go#L422)), which are:
"0-3,18-19,38-43,57-59,78-79" - "18-19,34-35,57-59,74-75" = "0-3,38-43,78-79"
the reusable CPUs "36,37,73,76,77" marked in step 1 are missing.

To fix this, I assume the approach is to update `defaultCpuSet` when finishing generating [cpuTopologyHints](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/cm/cpumanager/policy_static.go#L607)

@ffromani Thanks for the info, I think #94220 is more likely to fit in my case. 
I alse notice map `cpusToReuse[podUID]` is used to mark reusable cpu for each pod, when allocating cpu for a new container, `GetTopologyHints` calculate the cpu hints.

The reusable CPU from initContainer can only be used by appContainer from the same pod:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/cm/cpumanager/policy_static.go#L532
```
        // Get a list of reusable CPUs (e.g. CPUs reused from initContainers).
	// It should be an empty CPUSet for a newly created pod.
	reusable := p.cpusToReuse[string(pod.UID)]
```
e.g. If pod X with 3 core reusable CPU initContainer, these 3 core CPU won't be reuse by pod Y. In this case, 3 core CPU are missing and will never be used.
Can we reuse CPU from all the pods? The code will be like:
```
	reusable := cpuset.NewCPUSet()
	for podId, r := range p.cpusToReuse {
		reusable = reusable.Union(r)
	}
```

If memory serves (will review later), `reusableCPUs` is meant to hold CPUs which have been allocated to init container which can be reused (hence the name) to allocate to the app container, because when app container is admitted, all init containers (except sidecars) are done executing. Hence we can save the allocation step, at least partially, and reuse the set of cpus.

`cpu_manager_state` is not meant to be consumed by third parties (humans or machines) hence it may not reflect in real time the allocation state of the cpus; and there are bugs in this area, (see #107074).

Should it be needed, the supported way to get the current allocation of CPUs at any given time is to use the `podresources API`.

@ffromani 
I think I found the root cause:
- `pod A`'s init container is exited and app container starts to run
- `pod B` starts, it will GC by `removeStaleState()` the inactive containers before allocate CPU: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/cm/cpumanager/cpu_manager.go#L252

But removeStaleState() won't consider `pod A`'s init container as inactive container: [cpu_manager.go#L373](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/cm/cpumanager/cpu_manager.go#L373), so the reusable CPU set won't be updated to `defaultCpuSet` in cpu_manager_state. That's why some reusable CPUs are missing.

I suppose there could be 3 selective approaches to fix:
1. remove inactive, unrestartable init containers in GC `removeStaleState()` [cpu_manager.go#L252](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/cm/cpumanager/cpu_manager.go#L252)

it guarantees `defaultCpuSet` won't miss any reusbale CPUs, but I am not sure we should remove a init container when it's app container is still running.

2. update `defaultCpuSet` whenever the init container's cpuset be marked as reusable CPU [policy_static.go#L266](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/cm/cpumanager/policy_static.go#L266)

it also guarantees `defaultCpuSet` won't miss any reusbale CPUs.

3. share reusable CPU among all the pods. When a new pod comes in during `allocateCPUs()`, we provider all the reusable CPUs across all the pods [policy_static.go#L355](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/cm/cpumanager/policy_static.go#L355):

before:
```
// Allocate CPUs according to the NUMA affinity contained in the hint.
cpuset, err := p.allocateCPUs(s, numCPUs, hint.NUMANodeAffinity, p.cpusToReuse[string(pod.UID)])
```
after:
```
reusable := cpuset.New()
for _, r := range p.cpusToReuse {
	reusable = reusable.Union(r)
}
cpuset, err := p.allocateCPUs(s, numCPUs, hint.NUMANodeAffinity, reusable)
```
it only fixes when a new Pod encounters not enough CPU error due to reusable CPU missing in `defaultCpuSet`, it won't guarantee `defaultCpuSet` is right.

the issue looks legit and warrants further investigation

title: Higher CPU usage when pods are placed in a single namespace
body:
### What happened?

When @afcollins was testing with [benchmarking](https://github.com/cloud-bulldozer/kube-burner/blob/master/cmd/kube-burner/ocp-config/node-density-heavy/node-density-heavy.yml) runs, it was observed that we if place the pods in a single namespace the reported CPU usage is much higher than if we just distribute those pods across multiple namespaces. 

e.g. When all 6006 pods are created in the same namespace, the kubepods.slice exceeds 12 cores.
However, when dividing the same 6006 pods across 4 namespaces (capping each namespace to 2000 pods), the node's CPU maxes out at 5 cores.


![image](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/12152047/b4bffcb2-7ea5-4b89-bc20-30a66fe26dd3)

Corresponding prometheus query - `prom query:
sum by (id) (( rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{ job=~".*", id =~"/system.slice|/system.slice/kubelet.service|/system.slice/ovs-vswitchd.service|/system.slice/crio.service|/system.slice/systemd-journald.service|/system.slice/ovsdb-server.service|/system.slice/systemd-udevd.service|/kubepods.slice"}[$interval])) * 100 * on (node) group_left kube_node_role{ role = "worker" } )
`

This becomes an issue on smaller cloud nodes with 8vCPU, where the excessive CPU use causes the nodes to thrash, skip metrics collection, and presents as a poorly-performing workload. Changing the config to break iterations into namespaces allows the workload to run on the smaller cloud nodes.

The goal here is to understand why the CPU usage compounds when pods are focused in a single namespace and if that points to any performance improvements we can make.

![image](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/12152047/1856bfa0-8a5c-41c0-95ae-61e3e584f4ae)

Prometheus query - `sum( rate( (node_cpu_seconds_total{ mode != "idle" } * on (instance) group_left label_replace( kube_node_role{ role = "worker"} , "instance" , "$1" , "node" ,"(.*)") )[$interval:] ) ) by (instance) * 100
`

Memory, network, and memory demands on the node stay mostly constant. The only increase we see is CPU.


The observed higher CPU usage comes from the worker nodes, so none of the control plane components like API server, etcd are at play here. 



 

### What did you expect to happen?

CPU consumption should remain same whether we run the pods in single namespace or distribute them across multiple namespaces.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Get the kube-burner suite - https://github.com/cloud-bulldozer/kube-burner/tree/master
2. To run the pods in single namespace - `kube-burner ocp node-density-heavy --pods-per-node 150`
3. To run the pods in multiple namespaces - `kube-burner ocp node-density-heavy --pods-per-node 150 --iterations-per-namespace=10`

### Anything else we need to know?

Another run showed similar results, 

`kube-burner ocp node-density-heavy --pods-per-node 150` (single namespace)
vs.
`kube-burner ocp node-density-heavy --pods-per-node 150 --iterations-per-namespace=10` (multiple namespaces)

Results from 4 worker nodes. All CPU is coming from /kubepods.slice. (695 - 559 = 136 ) seconds less CPU  just by distributing into more namespaces -

Single namespace - 
`sum ( container_cpu_usage_seconds_total { id =~ "/system.slice|/system.slice/kubelet.service|/system.slice/ovs-vswitchd.service|/system.slice/crio.service|/kubepods.slice" } and on (node) kube_node_role{ role = "worker" } ) by ( id )`

```
/kubepods.slice: 36173 - 35478 = 695
/system.slice: 41456 - 41119 = 337
```

`sum ( node_cpu_seconds_total { } ) by ( mode )`
```
user: 265317 - 263848 = 1469
system: 66657 - 66229 = 428
irq: 25040 - 24951 = 89
softirq: 16627 - 16567 = 60
```
Multiple namespaces - 
`sum ( container_cpu_usage_seconds_total { id =~ "/system.slice|/system.slice/kubelet.service|/system.slice/ovs-vswitchd.service|/system.slice/crio.service|/kubepods.slice" } and on (node) kube_node_role{ role = "worker" } ) by ( id )`

```
/kubepods.slice: 37084 - 36525 = 559
/system.slice: 42439 - 42099 = 340
```

`sum ( node_cpu_seconds_total { } ) by ( mode )`
```
user: 269176 - 267809 = 1367
system: 67785 - 67360 = 425
irq: 25369 - 25277 = 92
softirq: 16848 - 16785 = 63
```

/cc @SergeyKanzhelev @pacoxu

/triage accepted

/sig instrumentation 
Could you please help us understand the issue here while we triage node side of things? Can this just be an issue on how metrics are reported?

/cc @dashpole 
for instrumentation support

> Could you please help us understand the issue here while we triage node side of things? Can this just be an issue on how metrics are reported?

This shouldn't be an issue with how the metrics are reported.  The metric in question is the CPU usage of the kubepods cgroup (kubepods.slice).  The cgroup's CPU usage is measured directly by cAdvisor, so there shouldn't be any aggregation issues.

It also seems incredibly unlikely to me that splitting into multiple namespaces would impact pod CPU usage at all.

@harche can you try and break down the kubepods cgroup usage into usage by individual pods?  Can you verify that there are the same number of total pods/containers reported via metrics?  If there are the same number, are there outliers in terms of CPU usage compared with other runs?
Is this related benchmark running script?  Can you briefly introduce about how it runs? Or how to reproduce it in a simple way?

After looking deeper into the logs from the runs, it seems it more related to multus-cni than k8s.

title: E2E - Sig-autoscaling: Refactor the Autoscaling utils to use `gomega.Consistenly`  according to e2e test framework guidance
body:
### What happened?

Originally from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/121861#discussion_r1392089576

There was a bug https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/121860 that caused test to fail, and `gomega.Consistenly` was  used to replace the code but requires more updates to the testing code to be used as intended.

>When using gomega.Consistently, you are making a statement about some observable fact. The callback should only deliver that fact, the statement then should be (no pun intended) in the Should. That way you get all the advantages listed in https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/devel/sig-testing/writing-good-e2e-tests.md#polling-and-timeouts.

> You also need to check error handling. Does `rc.GetReplicas` fail on errors? It would be better to return an error and let `Consistently` and `HandleRetry` deal with it.

 It fails hard with in its helper function after making the API call. If I understand correctly that isn't following the pattern suggested in https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/devel/sig-testing/writing-good-e2e-tests.md#polling-and-timeouts. either. 
 https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/1bb2773153d5d7395d445feb23171ad8b84afb13/test/e2e/framework/autoscaling/autoscaling_utils.go#L444-L452

title: Kubelet can generate an invalid fully qualified domain name for a pod
body:
Kubelet can generate an invalid fully qualified domain name for a pod when the `ClusterDomain` configured in the kubelets config.yaml defaults to ""

The code in function `GeneratePodHostNameAndDomain` can result in a fully qualified domain name ending in a period, which is invalid.

The problematic line is `hostDomain = fmt.Sprintf("%s.%s.svc.%s", pod.Spec.Subdomain, pod.Namespace, clusterDomain)`

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/36930f4cb605450ccbe3126caad365aa5f51267c/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go#L455

The code already has a check for length of subdomain string being > 0.  I wonder if a similar check for the ClusterDomain string would be sensible?

Note:  I believe that kubeadm will set `ClusterDomain` in the kubelets config to a non empty string, but it remains the case that the default of "" doesn't get handled well.  Id be happy to submit a fix, but would appreciate insights from an SME first.

looks like there is no defaulting for ClusterDomain in the kubelet, so "" is allowed.
if later the trailing dot can happen, then this is a bug, because there is no error checking around this scenario.

kubeadm defaults it to `cluster.local`
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/cmd/kubeadm/app/apis/kubeadm/types.go#L257C68-L258

i would like to support on this issue.

Before running for PRs I'd like to see a reproducer on the problem and what are the exact issues caused by 

> but it remains the case that the default of "" doesn't get handled well

why `pod.default.svc.` does not work?
I can see different places in the code that handles Clusterdomain empty
/remove-good-first-issue

After further investigation, Im going to close this issue.  According to wikipedia and other sources, it is valid for an FQDN to end in a period.  To quote from wikipedia 

```
The topmost layer of every domain name is the [DNS root zone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNS_root_zone), 
which is expressed as an empty label and can be represented in an FQDN with a trailing dot, such as 
somehost.example.com. .   A trailing dot is generally implied and often omitted by most applications.
```

The problem was seen when a hostname with this trailing period was sent over the CRI to a container runtime running on a different operating system (not linux or windows)

```
Warning  FailedCreatePodSandBox  62s (x5 over 2m32s)  kubelet  Failed to create pod 
sandbox: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = container create failed: runc create failed: 
unable to start container process: error during container init: sethostname: invalid argument.
```

I tried to recreate on linux but there the hostname is accepted and the container is created.  So this appears to be a difference in the implementation of the operating systems sethostname call. 

Id note that the `hostname` command on linux also doesn't like hostnames with a period as a suffix, but from what I can see that isn't used in containers.

Thanks to those that offered to help fix this.

-->

#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

For the volume statically provisioned by user who create the pv with an existing class, according to the current implementation of the findDeletablePlugin func, the func will return the an error if the volume does not be annotated with the pv.kubernetes.io/provisioned-by annotaion.

The annotation is automatically added to a pv that has been dynamically provsioned by either the pv controller or an external provisioner. Its value is name of volume plugin or provisioner that creates the volume. Its serves both user (to slow where a PV comes from) and Kubernetes (to recongize dynamically provisioned PVs in its decisions). 

If a pv is annotated and its annoation value doesn't contain the 'kuberentes.io/', the external provsioner will handle the pv when the pv is deleted after the pv is marked as Released. If a pv is not annotated, the pv controller will treat it as statically provisioned and try to find a in-tree plugin to handle it by volume spec. If no suitable plugin is found, the pv controller will mark the pv as failed with the error that is no deletable volume plugin matched.

In this issue, the pv is created by users with a csi type. So the volume won't be never annotated even through the pv has specified an existing storageclass. so when the pv is deleted, the pv controller will mark it as Failed.

the [KEP-2644](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-storage/2644-honor-pv-reclaim-policy) introduces a new finalizer `external-provisioner.volume.kubernetes.io/finalizer` to honor pv's reclaim policy whatever the pv is dynamically or statically provsioned. 

For statically provsioned pvs, if its volume source is csi, the pv controller cannot find a plugin by volume spec because this csi plugin does not implemenet the DeletableVolumePlugin interface. Those pvs deletion behavior is expected to be handled by the external provisioner. however, the current implement of the findDeletablePlugin func cannot recognize this situation and wrongly changes the volume phase from Release to Fail when the pv controller watches the pv deletion event or the resync period is reached, the pv is put into queue and then handle by the syncVolume func.

In the log pasted by @reenakabra, we can see that the external provsioner do delete pv and try to remove the finalizer but failed due to the resourceVersion conflict. even though the external provsioner retries its job but the pv phase may have been changed to Failed. Once a pv state is not Release, the external provisioner won't be able to remove the pv's finalizers in subsequent reconcile cycles. So the pv deletion will be stuck forever due to the finalizer existing.

In order to fix this issue, the findDeletablePlugin func should recongize the volume which may be able to handled by an external provioner when the volume source is csi or the pv has migrated annotation whatever the pv is dynamically or statically provsioned. 

With this patch, the pv controller won't changes PV's phase to Failed and the external provisioner can remove the finalizer in next reconcile loop. Unfortunately if the provious existing pv has the Failed state, this patch won't take effort. It requires users to remove finalizer.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

-->

title: daemonset pod cannot be created quickly, when some nodes are added to the cluster and controller-manager OOM will be triggered
body:
### What happened? ref: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/112319 【Question】 question 1: Now our k8s cluster has 5k nodes. When we expand some nodes in the k8s cluster, the daemonset pod cannot be created quickly. It takes about 2 hours to create the daemonset pod. Add a new node daemonset pod startup time: ![image](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/3377677/ef2d7885-1ce4-4e90-9340-205b00093f5f) ![image](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/3377677/5b0e4cb4-1fa2-470e-8eea-bb6e92c1002d) question 2: Look at the monitoring of `kube-controller-manager` Memory usage reaches 900GB and triggers OOM. `kube-controller-manager` memory usage monitoring: ![image](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/3377677/6b628b11-1676-4862-9616-07f99554ce36) 【Solution】 In a cluster with 5K nodes, we found that when the daemonset controller watches update `Node` events, due to the large number of `Node` events, the `NodeInformer` [pendingNotifications](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/3e438c54a77ccf7b9e0aff924eb977031099cc2f/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache/shared_informer.go#L876) ring buffer has more `Node` events to be processed, resulting in the Node EventHandler's `Add/Update` callback function being processed slowly. Affects the creation of daemonset pod and `kube-controller-manager` `OOM` issues. We optimized the [shouldIgnoreNodeUpdate](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/1d9e1e6d56cbd5c9d04ba25cccf184a973056a79/pkg/controller/daemon/daemon_controller.go#L693) logic in the [UpdateNode](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/1d9e1e6d56cbd5c9d04ba25cccf184a973056a79/pkg/controller/daemon/daemon_controller.go#L693) method of the daemonset controller `NodeInformer` to reduce unnecessary Node event processing: original code: ``` func shouldIgnoreNodeUpdate(oldNode, curNode v1.Node) bool { if !nodeInSameCondition(oldNode.Status.Conditions, curNode.Status.Conditions) { return false } oldNode.ResourceVersion = curNode.ResourceVersion oldNode.Status.Conditions = curNode.Status.Conditions return apiequality.Semantic.DeepEqual(oldNode, curNode) } ``` optimized code: ``` func shouldIgnoreNodeUpdate(oldNode, curNode v1.Node) bool { if !nodeInSameCondition(oldNode.Status.Conditions, curNode.Status.Conditions) { return false } oldNode.ResourceVersion = curNode.ResourceVersion oldNode.Status.Conditions = curNode.Status.Conditions + oldNode.Status.Images = curNode.Status.Images + oldNode.Status.NodeInfo = curNode.Status.NodeInfo + oldNode.Status.Capacity = curNode.Status.Capacity + oldNode.Status.Allocatable = curNode.Status.Allocatable return apiequality.Semantic.DeepEqual(oldNode, curNode) } func (dsc *DaemonSetsController) updateNode(old, cur interface{}) { oldNode := old.(*v1.Node) curNode := cur.(*v1.Node) + oldNodeCopy := oldNode.DeepCopy() + curNodeCopy := curNode.DeepCopy() if shouldIgnoreNodeUpdate(*oldNodeCopy, *curNodeCopy) { return } dsList, err := dsc.dsLister.List(labels.Everything()) if err != nil { klog.V(4).Infof("Error listing daemon sets: %v", err) return } // TODO: it'd be nice to pass a hint with these enqueues, so that each ds would only examine the added node (unless it has other work to do, too). for _, ds := range dsList { _, oldShouldSchedule, oldShouldContinueRunning, err := dsc.nodeShouldRunDaemonPod(oldNode, ds) if err != nil { klog.Errorf("Error old node %s should run daemon %s/%s pod: %v", oldNode.Name, ds.Namespace, ds.Name, err) continue } _, currentShouldSchedule, currentShouldContinueRunning, err := dsc.nodeShouldRunDaemonPod(curNode, ds) if err != nil { klog.Errorf("Error current node %s should run daemon %s/%s pod: %v", oldNode.Name, ds.Namespace, ds.Name, err) continue } if (oldShouldSchedule != currentShouldSchedule) || (oldShouldContinueRunning != currentShouldContinueRunning) { klog.V(4).Infof("enqueueing daemon set %s/%s for node %v.", ds.Namespace, ds.Name, curNode.Name) dsc.enqueueDaemonSet(ds) } } } ``` 【Effect】 After adding some nodes to the cluster, the daemonset pod can be quickly created, and the `kube-controller-manager` memory is controlled at about 20GB. ![image](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/3377677/5c9e3a0a-13ac-45c6-b722-d8a1c802b14b) ### What did you expect to happen? 1. When adding some nodes to the k8s cluster, daemonset pod can be created quickly because the node requires CNI daemonset pod. 2. kube-controller-manager needs to use less memory to prevent frequent `OOM`triggers. 3. We have optimized the `shouldIgnoreNodeUpdate` logic in the `updateNode` method of the daemonset controller `NodeInformer` to reduce unnecessary `Node `event processing. Is this optimization logic possible? ### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)? When the k8s cluster size reaches 5k, add new nodes to the cluster. ### Anything else we need to know? _No response_ ### Kubernetes version

title: Kubelet not create Symlink for configmap volume after restarted
body:
### What happened?

When kubelet is creating configmap volume  for a pod, it finished writing `timestamp` dir and made symlink to `..data`. At the same time, the kubelet is restarted, unfortunately the configmap item symlink is not created.

I think you have fallen into a poorly defined part of the DNS schema.

First, let's repro:

```
$ k -n datalake create service clusterip trino --tcp=80
service/trino created

$ k -n datalake create service clusterip minio --tcp=80
service/minio created

$ k -n datalake create service externalname datalake --external-name=minio.datalake.svc.cluster.local
service/datalake created

$ k -n datalake get svc
NAME       TYPE           CLUSTER-IP    EXTERNAL-IP                        PORT(S)   AGE
datalake   ExternalName   <none>        minio.datalake.svc.cluster.local   <none>    5m54s
minio      ClusterIP      10.0.142.29   <none>                             80/TCP    6m46s
trino      ClusterIP      10.0.153.81   <none>                             80/TCP    6m52s

$ k -n datalake run "test-$RANDOM" -ti --restart=Never --image=busybox cat /etc/resolv.conf
search datalake.svc.cluster.local svc.cluster.local cluster.local us-central1-b.c.thockin-dev.internal c.thockin-dev.internal google.internal
nameserver 10.0.0.10
options ndots:5

$ k -n datalake run "test-$RANDOM" -ti --restart=Never --image=thockin/dnsutils -- dig +search +short trino.datalake.svc.cluster.local
10.0.153.81

$ k -n datalake run "test-$RANDOM" -ti --restart=Never --image=thockin/dnsutils -- dig +search +short trino.datalake.svc
10.0.153.81

$ k -n datalake run "test-$RANDOM" -ti --restart=Never --image=thockin/dnsutils -- dig +search +short trino.datalake
minio.datalake.svc.cluster.local.
10.0.142.29
```

So you can see this is reproducible.  For completeness, the shortest name works:

```
$ k -n datalake run "test-$RANDOM" -ti --restart=Never --image=thockin/dnsutils -- dig +search +short trino
10.0.153.81
```

And the "problem" name works from another namespace:

```
$ k -n default run "test-$RANDOM" -ti --restart=Never --image=thockin/dnsutils -- dig +search +short trino.datalake
10.0.153.81
```

So the issue is that WITHIN THAT NAMESPACE, your query is ambiguous (sorry!)

By default, all names are subject to search-path expansion.  Unless you configure otherwise, that means:
1) `<query>.<this-namespace>.svc.<zone>`
2) `<query>.svc.<zone>`
3) `<query>.<zone>`
4) `<query>`

You seem to want `trino.datalake` to skip (1) and hit (2), but I think it will actually hit (1), because `<host>.<svc>.<ns>.svc.<suffix>` is a valid query, and seems to be matching

```
$ k -n datalake run "test-$RANDOM" -ti --restart=Never --image=thockin/dnsutils -- dig +search +showsearch +nocomments trino.datalake

; <<>> DiG 9.18.19-1~deb12u1-Debian <<>> +search +showsearch +nocomments trino.datalake
;; global options: +cmd
;trino.datalake.datalake.svc.cluster.local. IN A
trino.datalake.datalake.svc.cluster.local. 30 IN CNAME minio.datalake.svc.cluster.local.
minio.datalake.svc.cluster.local. 30 IN	A	10.0.142.29
;; Query time: 1 msec
;; SERVER: 10.0.0.10#53(10.0.0.10) (UDP)
;; WHEN: Thu Feb 01 19:47:22 UTC 2024
;; MSG SIZE  rcvd: 217
```

Note the DNS question is "trino.datalake.datalake.svc.cluster.local." which is being satisfied by the CNAME (external-name) for datalake.datalake.svc.cluster.local.

But why?  Let's look at the spec: https://github.com/kubernetes/dns/blob/master/docs/specification.md#25---records-for-external-name-services

It actually only specifies a CNAME record for  `<service>.<ns>.svc.<zone>.`  To my eyes, that SHOULD NOT match, but CNAMEs have sometimes surprising semantics.

@chrisohaver - can you shed some light, maybe?
This errant behavior was fixed in https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/6162 and should be in the latest coredns release 1.11.1
YAY!

title: Critical: Node reboot could lead to data loss due to broken volume lifecycle management
body:
### What happened?

In certain situations, rebooting a Kubernetes node could lead to:
- Best case: A volume not getting mounted, despite it being a healthy volume
- Worse case: A volume getting mounted in an (ephemeral) empty host directory
- Worst cast: The wrong volume getting mounted inside the pod

### What did you expect to happen?

The right volume must be mounted in the right pod.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

- Create a PVC, and make sure all ongoing pod creations happen on the same node
- Create a deployment with long termination grace period, say 600 seconds, that uses that PVC, wait for it to become Ready
- Delete the deployment, which should result in the pod getting stuck in `Terminating` state
- Create another deployment that uses the same PVC
- Reboot the underlying node

After the reboot, one of the two happens:
- CSI node driver receives `NodePublishVolume` before receiving any `NodeStageVolume` requests, meaning the CSI will try to `Publish` using an invalid stage directory, which could lead to the CSI not being able to publish it (Best case) or it mounting the wrong volume (Worst case)
- CSI node driver does not receive any requests, and kubelet goes ahead and mounts the empty directory inside the pod, leading to the "Worse case" scenario described above.

These steps almost always results in one of the undesired outcomes to happen.

### Anything else we need to know?

After realizing that the issue was a regression, we bisected it, and it looks like this was first introduced in 1.23.15. We've verified that the issue disappears after downgrading node's kubelet to 1.23.14, but 1.23 and 1.24 have reached their EOL already.
Based on the history of changes on kubelet's volume manager code, the issue might've had been introduced in [this commit range](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/compare/75b8b1ebfd55e1c5042cdc33d3f30d8080bd707e%5E...390fc21359561b9094eff93e60176e244f3af54b).

### Kubernetes version

All currently supported kubelet versions (> 1.25) are affected.

kind: ClusterConfiguration

kind: KubeletConfiguration
apiVersion: kubelet.config.k8s.io/v1beta1

clusterCIDR: "10.244.0.0/16"
mode: ipvs

it's means When the network card has an ipv6 address, ensure that kube-proxy will not use the ipv6 address

> > The kube-proxy static pod abnormal exits. This featureGates does not seem to be recognized.
> 
> don't use the gate, just pass ip4 addresses to all components including kubelet.
> 
> also check this doc https://kubernetes.io/docs/setup/production-environment/tools/kubeadm/dual-stack-support/

works for me, thx
/assign @shaneutt
Should this be closed, then?

It seems like this should potentially be closed, but when we discussed this one on the SIG network sync today, @danwinship made a point that seems appropriate to bring up here:

```
FTR `--bind-address 0.0.0.0` *does not* disable IPv6. Kube-proxy will always run dual-stack on Linux unless ip6tables is unavailable.
```
